slides.title: Racing your first short track meet?
slides.sub: The racing is the easy part. Know the day around it.

slides.title: Enter honestly, and not too much
slides.body: If you have never been timed, say so rather than guessing a seed time. Two distances is plenty for a first meet.

slides.title: Arrive 90 minutes early
slides.body: Sign on first, then find where the start list goes up and where skaters are called from, before your boots are half laced.

slides.title: The kit check
slides.body: Helmet, cut resistant neck and ankle protection, gloves, knee and shin protection, undersuit. Pack it before you leave home.

slides.title: Use the warm up to read the ice
slides.body: Feel how the edges bite, take a few corners near race speed, and note where the track markers sit.

slides.title: Expect long gaps
slides.body: Heats in the morning and a final late in the afternoon is normal. Warm layers on as you leave the ice, eat little and often, keep moving gently.

slides.text: A skater who misses a call is not in the race.
